parts.visual:
A startup raises $2 Million. The founders celebrate. They hire 10 engineers, rent a fancy office, and buy MacBooks for everyone. Their monthly expenses are $200,000. They are making $0 in revenue. The CEO suddenly realizes that in exactly 10 months, the bank account will hit $0 and the company will die.

The Countdown:
1. Burn Rate: The exact amount of cash a company loses every single month. (If expenses are $200k and revenue is $50k, the 'Net Burn' is $150k per month).
2. Runway: The amount of time (in months) until the company runs out of cash. (Total Cash in Bank / Monthly Net Burn = Runway).
parts.audio: Startups do not die when they have a bad idea. Startups die when they run out of cash. Your 'Runway' is your oxygen level in space. If you do not track your runway every single week, you are a negligent CEO.

questions.question: A startup has $1.2 Million in the bank. They spend $150,000 a month on salaries and servers. They make $50,000 a month in revenue. What is their exact Runway?
options: 12 months. Their 'Net Burn' is $100,000 ($150k expenses minus $50k revenue). $1.2 Million divided by $100k equals 12 months. In exactly 365 days, they will go bankrupt if nothing changes.
questions.correct_answer: 12 months. Their 'Net Burn' is $100,000 ($150k expenses minus $50k revenue). $1.2 Million divided by $100k equals 12 months. In exactly 365 days, they will go bankrupt if nothing changes.
questions.explanation: Net Burn determines your survival, not Gross Expenses.

questions.question: Listen to the VC advising the founder. When should the founder start raising their next round of funding?
questions.tts_text: Do not wait until you have 2 months of runway left. Fundraising takes 6 months. If you start raising when you have 2 months of oxygen, VCs will smell your desperation, offer you terrible terms, and bleed you dry.
options: When they have 9 to 12 months of runway left. You must fundraise when you still have power. If you wait until you are out of cash, the VC has 100% of the leverage and will take massive chunks of your equity.
questions.correct_answer: When they have 9 to 12 months of runway left. You must fundraise when you still have power. If you wait until you are out of cash, the VC has 100% of the leverage and will take massive chunks of your equity.
questions.explanation: Always raise money when you don't desperately need it.

questions.question: What is the difference between 'Gross Burn' and 'Net Burn'?
options: Gross Burn is the total amount of money leaving the bank account (e.g., $100k). Net Burn is the total money leaving MINUS the revenue coming in (e.g., $100k - $20k revenue = $80k Net Burn). Net burn is the only metric that matters for survival.
questions.correct_answer: Gross Burn is the total amount of money leaving the bank account (e.g., $100k). Net Burn is the total money leaving MINUS the revenue coming in (e.g., $100k - $20k revenue = $80k Net Burn). Net burn is the only metric that matters for survival.

questions.question: What is the fastest, most effective way for a CEO to 'extend the runway' during a crisis?
options: Layoffs (Firing people). It is brutal, but in a software startup, 80% of expenses are human salaries. If a CEO needs to magically add 6 months to the runway to survive a recession, they must cut headcount aggressively.
questions.correct_answer: Layoffs (Firing people). It is brutal, but in a software startup, 80% of expenses are human salaries. If a CEO needs to magically add 6 months to the runway to survive a recession, they must cut headcount aggressively.
questions.explanation: Salaries are the heaviest weight on the airplane.
